Advanced tips and tricks

Source: vignettes/advanced_code.Rmd
advanced_code.Rmd

This document serves as a clearinghouse for nifty code chunks that might look complicated, but get a lot done.

library(otndata)
otn_login("act")
#> ✔ Login successful!

Database operations on the fly

Plone does not allow you to stream data over HTTP, but you can download files to a temporary directory and make some quick queries. Is this efficient? Maybe, maybe not. Here is an example:

td <- file.path(tempdir(), "detections")
dir.create(td)

otn_list_projects("mine", network = "act") |>
  _$collectioncode |>
  lapply(otn_extract_files, text = "matched parquet", network = "act") |>
  do.call(rbind, args = _) |>
  otn_download(outdir = td)
#> ✔ 5 file(s) saved to '

db <- arrow::open_dataset(td)
db |>
  dplyr::count(contactPI) |>
  dplyr::arrange(-n) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 54 × 2
#>    contactPI                                            n
#>    <chr>                                            <int>

otndo reports

Create reports for all of my projects in one go. Right now, this needs to be done separately for receiver and tag projects. First, receiver projects:

# List my projects
otn_list_projects("mine") |>

  # Grab the collection code
  _$collectioncode |>

  # Create receiver summaries, wrapped in tryCatch as some projects are tag-only
  lapply(
    function(x) {
      tryCatch(
        otn_receiver_summary(x),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
    }
  )

Same thing for tag projects:

# List my projects
otn_list_projects("mine") |>

  # Grab the collection code
  _$collectioncode |>

  # Create tag summaries, wrapped in tryCatch as some projects are receiver-only
  lapply(
    function(x) {
      tryCatch(
        otn_tag_summary(x),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
    }
  )

Multi-network users

List all of my extract files in parquet format projects across multiple networks.

c("act", "otn_devel") |>

  # List all of my projects
  lapply(
    function(.) otn_list_projects(what = "mine", network = .)
  ) |>
  do.call(rbind, args = _) |>

  # Pull out project codes
  _$collectioncode |>

  # Grab the parquet extract files. Wrapped in "tryCatch" in case some projects
  #    lack files
  lapply(
    function(x) {
      tryCatch(
        otn_extract_files(x, text = "parquet"),
        error = function(e) {
          NULL
        }
      )
    }
  ) |>
  do.call(rbind, args = _)
